Zimbabwe Implements Temporary Ban on Imported Construction Materials, Real Estate Sector Faces Immediate Impact

Harare – Zimbabwe’s Ministry of Trade and Industry has instituted a temporary ban on the importation of key construction materials used in real estate development, in a move officials say is aimed at boosting domestic manufacturing. The measure, effective since last week, restricts imports of cement, steel beams, and prefabricated panels, items heavily relied upon by the country’s real estate developers.

The Zimbabwe Real Estate Association (ZREA) has voiced concern over the ban’s immediate impact. “Several ongoing development projects have already reported delays due to difficulties in sourcing essential materials locally,” said ZREA spokesperson Tendai Moyo. “Firms are now revising construction timelines and renegotiating contracts with their clients.” 

Major developers, including Sunrise Estates and Platinum Holdings, have confirmed disruptions at multiple sites in Harare and Bulawayo, where work on residential and commercial complexes has slowed or halted. “We are operating at about 60% capacity on our active projects,” said a senior manager at Platinum Holdings. “Securing local supplies is proving challenging and prices have increased, which is impacting our budget forecasts.”

Industry analysts estimate that employment in the sector could decline by up to 15% if the restrictions persist, with casual laborers and skilled trades already reporting reduced shifts. “There’s uncertainty among workers, and some have seen their hours cut this week,” said Nyasha Chikafu, a labor union representative.

Government officials maintain that the measure is temporary and under review. “We are monitoring the situation and will adjust the policy as needed to balance sector stability and domestic industry growth,” said Deputy Trade Minister Portia Mutsvairo at a press briefing.

As the ban continues, real estate companies are seeking alternative sourcing strategies, while stakeholders await further guidance from authorities regarding the duration of the restrictions.
